main_text.p: illud unum utcunq; admonitos omnes velim, ut summam & coronidem totius hujus differtationis de Juramenti sensu & interpretatione, magnopere ut ca-veant, ne sibi nimium hac in re indulgeant; neu benigna nimis & laxa interpretatione, dum cupiditatibus suis plus æquo favent, Juramenti religionem minuant, & se perjurii periculo exponant. Atque hæc de Formali Causa dicta sufficiant.
main_text.head: SECT. XIV.
main_text.p: Causa 52De Finali Causa paucula restant dicenda. Dubium Primum est, cum promittitur res ex se licita, sed aut mala intentione, aut ob malum finem. Dicendum primo, simpliciter illicitum esse promittere aliquid quantumvis in se licitum, malo fine vel intentione. Ratio est, quia cum quivis unus defectus in quolibet actu humano sufficiat ad hoc, ut totus actus sit malus, (Bonum enim ex causa integra est, malum ex partiali:) tum præcipue defectus ex parte finis, ut qui in moralibus primas tenet partes; quo fere putant id Christi dictum pertinere, Si oculus tuus fuerit nequam, & totum corpus tenebrosum erit. Dicendum fe-
{a} Si oculus tuus fuerit nequam, & totum corpus tenebrosum erit. Mat.6.13

page.notes: The Latin note "Cafus 52" in the right margin is a side heading, read as "Causa 52" from the scan; the printed word may be "Cafus" (long s), so it is transcribed as "Causa" in the note text and should be checked. The scripture reference beside the foot line is marked "a" and is read as "Mat.6.13". The Greek-free text has no doubtful words; the foot line's italic runs across the column and is placed after the main text. The paragraph "Dicendum fe-" continues onto the next page.
